# cran-comments.md — nirs4allio

Maintainer: Grégory Beurier (CIRAD) <gregory.beurier@cirad.fr>

## Submission summary

* This is a **new submission**.
* `nirs4allio` is a thin R binding for the Rust-first `nirs4all-io`
  dataset-assembly bridge of the nirs4all NIRS / spectroscopy ecosystem. It
  exposes the stable `n4io_*` C ABI to R: normalize arbitrary inputs into a
  canonical `DatasetSpec` (`n4io_to_spec`), infer a scored `DatasetPlan`
  (`n4io_infer`), validate a `DatasetSpec` (`n4io_validate`), and report the ABI
  version (`n4io_abi_version`). The low-level surface is JSON-string in /
  JSON-string out; an idiomatic `nio_*` layer accepts native R inputs (a path, a
  vector of files, or a config list) and returns typed S3 objects.
* The package is a small **C shim** (`src/n4io.c`) over the C ABI. It compiles
  the `nirs4all-io` Rust core into a **static library** at install time and links
  it into `nirs4allio.{so,dll}`, so the installed package is self-contained — no
  prebuilt shared library and no `N4IO_CAPI_DIR` env var (the previous,
  non-CRAN-submittable form linked a separately built `libnirs4all_io_capi`
  cdylib).
* **Source tarball: ~3.6 MB** (≈3.76 MB; the exact byte count jitters slightly
  with the `xz` vendor archive) — well under CRAN's 10 MB soft cap.
  The crates.io dependency closure is shipped compressed (`vendor.tar.xz`); the
  test-only `[dev-dependencies]` and the header-generation `[build-dependencies]`
  (`cbindgen`) are stripped from the vendored manifests, keeping the vendor tree
  lean (53 crates).
* `R CMD check --as-cran`: **0 ERRORs, 0 WARNINGs**; only environment- /
  toolchain-specific NOTEs (detailed below).
* License: `CeCILL-2.1 | AGPL-3`.
* The same Rust core powers the project's Python (PyPI),
  JavaScript / WebAssembly (npm), MATLAB / Octave and C-ABI bindings.

## Self-contained source tarball

The package vendors **everything it needs to build offline**, so CRAN's build
farm never touches the network and needs no out-of-tree sources:

* `src/rust/vendored/` — the three workspace crates the C ABI needs
  (`nirs4all-io-core`, `nirs4all-io`, `nirs4all-io-capi`), copied verbatim from
  the project's repository (including the core crate's `conventions/builtin/*.toml`
  data files, which the Rust pulls in via `include_str!`). In the repo these are
  reached by relative `path =` dependencies; that is rewritten to in-tarball paths
  by `./configure`, which emits a self-contained `src/rust/Cargo.toml` workspace
  root re-declaring `[workspace.package]` / `[workspace.dependencies]`.
* `src/nirs4all_io.h` — the committed C ABI header the shim `#include`s, copied
  from the capi crate by `./configure`. The header is generated by `cbindgen`
  upstream and pinned here; the R build never re-runs `cbindgen` (its build
  script and build-dependency are dropped from the vendored capi), so the entire
  `cbindgen` / `clap` / `syn` / `getrandom` / `rustix` closure stays out of the
  tarball.
* `src/rust/vendor.tar.xz` — every crates.io transitive dependency, produced by
  `cargo vendor` and shipped **compressed** (`xz`, as the CRAN "Using Rust"
  guidance recommends). `src/Makevars` / `src/Makevars.win` extract it and build
  offline against it, passing the crates.io source replacement INLINE to cargo
  (`cargo build --offline --config source.crates-io.replace-with="vendored-sources"
  --config source.vendored-sources.directory="vendor"`). The replacement is
  passed inline rather than via a `.cargo/config.toml` so the package ships no
  hidden `.cargo/` directory. The deps are shipped as an archive rather than a
  raw directory because `R CMD build`'s tarball step strips VCS dotfiles from
  inside vendored crates, which would otherwise break cargo's offline checksum
  verification — the same pattern the `gifski` and `prqlr` CRAN packages use for
  their Rust vendor trees.

Per CRAN's "Using Rust" policy, `src/Makevars` and `src/Makevars.win` pass
`-j 2` to every `cargo build`, bounding Cargo's parallelism rather than letting
it default to every logical CPU on the build machine.

The `Cargo` / `rustc` toolchain is declared in `SystemRequirements`.

## Windows / UCRT toolchain

On Windows the Rust core is compiled for the `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` target so
its ABI matches Rtools' mingw-w64 gcc (which performs the final link of the Rust
archive into `nirs4allio.dll`). The static library is referenced by exact path
and the Rust-std native system libs (`-lkernel32 -lntdll -luserenv -lws2_32
-ldbghelp -lgcc`) are appended after it (mingw `ld` is order-sensitive). Rtools45
ships no separate `libgcc_eh.a` — the unwinder, `__gcc_personality_seh0`, and
`__chkstk` live inside `libgcc.a` — so `-lgcc` (not `-lgcc_eh`) resolves them; a
`libgcc_mock/libgcc_eh.a` shim is kept on `LIBRARY_PATH` defensively.

## Test environments

* Local development (Ubuntu 22.04 / WSL2, R 4.6.0 conda-forge, rustc 1.95):
  standalone offline install of the built source tarball with
  `CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true` (no network, no access to the repository `crates/`)
  -> installs and loads cleanly; the native C-ABI path is active (the smoke test
  drives `to_spec` / `infer` / `validate` and the idiomatic `nio_*` layer through
  the offline-built static library and reports `R binding smoke OK`).
* Submission-grade checks run on **current R (release + devel)** before upload
  via the GitHub Actions matrix (`.github/workflows/release-r.yml`):
  - Ubuntu 22.04 (R release + devel)
  - macOS 14 (R release, arm64)
  - Windows Server 2022 (R release)
* win-builder and R-hub v2 are run manually before each CRAN submission.

## R CMD check --as-cran status

`R CMD check --as-cran` (R 4.6.0 conda-forge) finishes with **0 ERRORs and
0 WARNINGs**. The NOTEs are:

1. **CRAN incoming feasibility — "New submission" + Title case.** Always present
   for a first upload. The title-case sub-note flags `nirs4all` in the Title; that
   is the product / project name, intentionally lower-case (the GitHub
   organisation, the PyPI package, and the C library all spell it `nirs4all`), so
   it is left as written.
2. **Compilation flag `-march=nocona`.** Comes from conda-forge R's own
   `Makeconf` (`CFLAGS`), not from the package. The package's `src/Makevars` sets
   only `PKG_CPPFLAGS = -I.` (the committed-header include dir); the Cargo release
   profile sets only `opt-level = 2`. This NOTE does **not** appear on a vanilla
   (non-conda) R build such as CRAN's.
3. **checking compiled code.** On the local conda-forge toolchain R's
   `tools::checkFF` symbol-table reader fails to parse the large static Rust
   archive (`Error in tab[, "name"] : incorrect number of dimensions`), because
   conda's `nm` emits "no symbols" for the bundled `compiler_builtins` objects.
   This is a parser failure in the local conda toolchain, not a finding about the
   package, and is absent on CRAN's GNU binutils. On CRAN's Debian builder the
   equivalent check may instead report the standard Rust-static-library `abort`
   reference (std's panic / allocation-failure paths) — inherent to linking any
   Rust dependency tree, not a defect in the package's own code.

`src/Makevars(.win)` prune the extracted `vendor/` tree and the cargo
build-script scratch (`$(LIBDIR)/build`) immediately after linking, so R CMD
check does not scan third-party build artefacts the package compiles but does not
author.

## Anti-patterns avoided

* No `-O3`, `-march=native`, `-Werror`, or other non-portable compiler flags.
  The Cargo release profile uses `opt-level = 2` only.
* No internet access during configure, install, examples, or tests
  (`cargo build --offline` against the bundled `vendor/`).
* No filesystem writes outside the build / `tempdir()` tree (the smoke test
  writes its tiny fixtures under `tempdir()`).
* No `:::` calls to private functions of other packages.
* Only `jsonlite` is imported; the package is a leaf in the CRAN dependency graph.
* `cargo build` parallelism is bounded with `-j 2` per CRAN's "Using Rust"
  policy.

```text
This is a new submission.

nirs4allio is a thin R binding for the Rust-first nirs4all-io dataset-assembly
bridge for the nirs4all NIRS / spectroscopy ecosystem. It exposes the stable
n4io_* C ABI to R: normalize arbitrary inputs into a canonical DatasetSpec,
infer a DatasetPlan, validate a DatasetSpec, and materialize a bytes-free
assembled structural summary. The low-level surface is JSON in / JSON out; an
idiomatic nio_* layer accepts native R inputs and returns typed S3 objects.
License: CeCILL-2.1 | AGPL-3.

Self-contained source tarball: the package vendors the nirs4all-io Rust core and
its crates.io transitive dependencies (shipped compressed as vendor.tar.xz) and
compiles them OFFLINE into a static library at install time via
src/Makevars(.win) (no network, no external repository crates/). The C ABI
header is committed (src/nirs4all_io.h). The Cargo / rustc toolchain is declared
in SystemRequirements.

Test environments: local Ubuntu/WSL2 R 4.6.0 (offline standalone install ->
installs, loads, native path active, smoke passes); CI matrix (release-r.yml) on
Ubuntu 22.04 (R release + devel), macOS 14 (R release, arm64), Windows Server
2022 (R release); win-builder + R-hub v2 run manually before submission.

R CMD check --as-cran: 0 ERRORs, 0 WARNINGs. The NOTEs are the first-submission
note (with a title-case sub-note on the product name "nirs4all", intentionally
lower-case) and local conda-toolchain artefacts (-march=nocona from conda's
Makeconf; an nm symbol-table parser quirk on the static Rust archive) that do not
occur on CRAN's toolchain. The package does no network access during
install/examples/tests and imports only jsonlite.

Maintainer: Grégory Beurier (CIRAD), gregory.beurier@cirad.fr.
```

## Reviewer-facing notes

* The vendored core crates under `src/rust/vendored/` are an exact textual copy
  of `crates/nirs4all-io-core`, `crates/nirs4all-io`, and `crates/nirs4all-io-capi`
  from the project's GitHub repository at the commit matching this version
  (`build.rs` and the test-only / `cbindgen` dependency tables removed). The
  vendoring is automated by `bindings/r/configure` (`N4IO_R_VENDOR=1`) and is the
  same step the `release-r.yml` CI and the R-universe `.prepare` hook run before
  `R CMD build`.
* Maintainer is Grégory Beurier (CIRAD, `gregory.beurier@cirad.fr`).

Thank you for the review!
